📸 201 Aniversario de la Consolidación de la Independencia en la Mar — Ciudad de México, 23 de noviembre de 2026

🇲🇽⚓ "Independence was not a gift or a concession. It was a conquest by those who dared to fight for a free nation." "Today, as two centuries ago, we have the determination to keep building our own path with dignity, with independence, with justice, and with the conviction that Mexico's destiny is decided only by the people of Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, 201st anniversary of the Consolidation of Independence at Sea, Mexico City, Nov 23, 2026 Sheinbaum honored the Navy, from the first naval squadron that blockaded San Juan de Ulúa in 1825 to today's force: Mexican-developed unmanned aircraft for surveillance, secure radio and communication systems, oceanographic and weather buoys in the Pacific to improve hurricane forecasts and early warning, sargassum cleanup in the Caribbean, and the modernization of ports.

🇲🇽☕ "Nestlé has to pay what it has to pay for the coffee, for the kilo of coffee." "It can't be that the market sets the price of coffee for the coffee growers, even through intermediaries (...) The coffee growers are right and we are going to support them." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 25, 2026 Coffee growers in Tapachula, Chiapas, protested against the multinational. According to the question, they are being paid 43 pesos, and 165,000 families depend on the crop. Sheinbaum said coffee is sold at 580 pesos and bought at 43, and the growers are asking for 50 to 60 pesos. She said that since yesterday she has instructed Agriculture Secretary Columba López to back the growers in their negotiation with the company and to go to Chiapas. "Nestlé has to pay, and it has to buy directly from the producers."

🚨🇲🇽 "We collaborate, we do not subordinate ourselves, and we do not share this vision of terrorism regarding organized crime groups." "When President Trump declared organized crime groups terrorists, we said at that moment, and we stand by it, that this cannot be an argument for interference or intervention in Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 25, 2026 On November 20, at the OAS Permanent Council, 12 member states, which the reporter noted are the same ones that make up Trump's "Shield of the Americas", voted to convene the consultation body of the Inter-American Treaty of Reciprocal Assistance (TIAR) to fight drug cartels as "narco-terrorists." Mexico's representative Alejandro Encinas rejected it, and Sheinbaum fully backed him. Mexico amended articles 40 and 19 of its Constitution to strengthen non-intervention and "collaboration without subordination." Does the treaty have implications for Mexico? "It shouldn't, because it is not above our Constitution."

🇲🇽🌎 "We have a free trade agreement with the United States, we don't have one with China, but we have a lot of trade with China. So we want to export more to China." "Imports, not only from China, from various countries, reduced the productive capacity of several sectors in the country. And our interest is that more is produced in Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 25, 2026 Correcting a reporter, Sheinbaum said there were no agreements at her meeting with Xi Jinping in Shenzhen: "a very good meeting, with a lot of communication, frank dialogue." Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard then met his Chinese counterpart about opening China to more Mexican exports, from agricultural products up, and a working group is being set up. China's CRRC is already building the México–Pachuca trains in Ciudad Sahagún. On the trip, she said, Mexico sought to convey "republican austerity, honesty and love for the people."
